title: Three kinds of undo
setup: git init -q . && git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main
printf 'line one\n' > notes.txt && git add notes.txt && git commit -qm 'Add notes'
printf 'print hello\n' > app.txt && git add app.txt && git commit -qm 'Add app'
printf 'password=1234\n' > bad.txt && git add bad.txt && git commit -qm 'Add secret password file'
printf 'not ready yet\n' > draft.txt && git add draft.txt

checks.name: draft.txt still exists but is not staged or committed
checks.cmd: test -f draft.txt && git diff --cached --quiet && test -z "$(git ls-files draft.txt)"

checks.name: notes.txt is back to its committed content
history is kept: there are now 4 commits
the newest commit is a revert

hints: Order matters: git revert needs a clean staging area, so unstage draft.txt first.
git restore --staged draft.txt unstages. git restore notes.txt discards the edit.
git revert --no-edit HEAD makes a new commit that reverses the last one.
